reason: The cited evidence shows that rapid annealing was applied after 50% hot + 70% cold rolling (E3) and that a hybrid process achieved high strength and ductility (E2), but none of the passages directly demonstrate that rapid annealing alone refines colonies, relieves stresses, or improves interface quality in a way that simultaneously enhances both properties relative to an unannealed baseline. E1 describes crack-arresting aligned lamellae after heavy rolling, not the effect of annealing. The key mechanistic and outcome premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Rapid annealing after >50% rolling refines lamellar colonies in AlCoCrFeNi2.1
Refined colonies simultaneously increase strength and room-temperature ductility
Rapid annealing relieves residual stresses and promotes partial recrystallization/ordering at phase boundaries
Improved interface quality reduces microcrack nucleation sites
The effect requires >50% rolling reduction and a specific annealing window (15 K/s, ~700 °C, 30–50 s)
